name: Jai Mahal Palace
top_review: Stunning heritage property. Peacocks roam the garden and the Rajput architecture is breathtaking. Food is excellent. Service is warm and attentive. Highly recommended for a royal Rajasthan experience.
dietary_options: vegetarian, vegan on request, Jain on advance notice
text: Jai Mahal Palace is a luxury 5-star heritage hotel in Jaipur's Civil Lines area. Built in 1745, it sits on 18 acres of Mughal gardens. Rating 4.6/5 from 1840+ reviews. Amenities include outdoor pool, Aurica spa, Suvarna Mahal restaurant (award-winning), 24hr service. Price approx ₹12,000–25,000/night. Ideal for honeymoons and premium travellers. Close to Rambagh Palace. Peacocks in grounds, heritage decor throughout.

name: Zostel Jaipur
top_review: Best budget stay in Jaipur. Social vibe, great rooftop, helpful staff who give genuine local tips. Dorms are clean with good lockers. 5-minute walk to good food.
text: Zostel Jaipur is a top-rated budget hostel on MI Road in central Jaipur. Rating 4.3/5 from 3200+ reviews. Dormitory beds from ₹450/night, private rooms from ₹1200. Rooftop hangout space, common kitchen, free WiFi, locker storage. Excellent for solo travellers and backpackers. Well connected to Jaipur Junction railway station (10 min auto). Rooftop has Hawa Mahal views. Staff known for local knowledge. Very popular — book 3–5 days in advance.

name: Pearl Palace Heritage
address: 51 Hari Kishan Somani Marg, Hathroi Fort, Jaipur 302001
top_review: Fantastic value for money. Every room is themed differently — ours had hand-painted walls. Rooftop restaurant has the best thali in Jaipur. Free airport pickup sealed the deal.
text: Pearl Palace Heritage is an award-winning mid-range heritage hotel in Jaipur. Rating 4.5/5 from 2900 reviews. Rooms from ₹2800/night, includes complimentary breakfast and airport/station pickup. Each room uniquely hand-painted in Rajasthani art style. Rooftop Peacock Restaurant is famous for dal baati churma and thalis (rated among best in city). Located near Hathroi Fort, easy access to MI Road markets and Old City. Free WiFi, AC, hot water. Won multiple Travel Awards. Great for families and couples.

name: Taj Lake Palace
top_review: A once-in-a-lifetime experience. Waking up surrounded by Lake Pichola with the Aravalli hills in the distance is magical. The Jiva Spa and Neel Kamal restaurant are exceptional. Staff anticipate every need.
text: Taj Lake Palace, Udaipur is one of India's most iconic luxury hotels — floating on Lake Pichola. Rating 4.7/5. Rooms from ₹35,000/night. Boat transfer from Bansi Ghat included. Neel Kamal restaurant serves royal Mewari cuisine. Jiva Spa, pool, heritage rooms with lake views. This is the hotel from the James Bond film Octopussy. Best booked 2-3 months in advance for peak season (Oct–Feb). Featured in every top India hotel list. Truly a bucket-list property.

name: Krishna Niwas Guest House
address: Near Jagdish Temple, Old City, Udaipur 313001
top_review: Incredible value. Lake view from the rooftop cafe is stunning — better than hotels charging 10x the price. Simple clean rooms, very friendly family-run atmosphere.
text: Krishna Niwas is a beloved budget guesthouse in Udaipur's Old City, steps from Jagdish Temple and Lake Pichola. Rating 4.4/5 from 1600+ reviews. Rooms from ₹700/night. Rooftop cafe with breathtaking lake and City Palace views. Family-run, warm hospitality, free WiFi, hot water. Perfect for backpackers and budget-conscious travellers who want old-city charm. Book at least a week ahead in peak season.

name: Fateh Prakash Palace
top_review: Staying inside the City Palace complex is surreal. The Crystal Gallery is extraordinary. Sunset from the terrace restaurant over Lake Pichola — unforgettable.
dietary_options: vegetarian, vegan, Jain on advance request
text: Fateh Prakash Palace is a luxury heritage hotel within the City Palace complex in Udaipur. Rating 4.5/5. Rooms from ₹18,000/night. Direct access to Crystal Gallery (world-renowned Victorian crystal collection). Sunset Terrace restaurant with Lake Pichola panorama. Heritage rooms with royal Rajput decor. Managed by the Royal Family of Mewar. Exceptional for those who want palace-life immersion. The Sunset Terrace afternoon tea is highly reviewed.

name: RAAS Jodhpur
address: Tunwarji Ka Jhalra, Makrana Mohalla, Jodhpur 342001
top_review: The most photogenic hotel I've ever stayed in. Waking up to Mehrangarh Fort lit up at sunrise from your private terrace is breathtaking. Darikhana restaurant serves exceptional Rajasthani food.
dietary_options: vegetarian, vegan options, Jain on request
text: RAAS Jodhpur is an award-winning design-luxury hotel at the foot of Mehrangarh Fort in the Blue City. Rating 4.6/5 from 1200 reviews. Rooms from ₹16,000/night. Direct fort and Blue City views from all rooms. Infinity pool, Darikhana fine-dining restaurant, Dune Spa. Walking distance from fort, Toorji step-well, Sardar Market. Won Condé Nast Traveller awards multiple years. Excellent for photography, romance, culture immersion. The rooftop cocktail hour at sunset is famous.

name: Zostel Jodhpur
address: Near Clock Tower, Old City, Jodhpur 342001
top_review: The rooftop fort view is UNREAL for this price. Staff helped book blue city walking tour and were incredibly helpful. Clean dorms. The morning chai on the rooftop with fort views = perfection.
text: Zostel Jodhpur is the best budget hostel in Jodhpur Old City with direct Mehrangarh Fort views. Rating 4.4/5 from 2200 reviews. Dorms from ₹500, private rooms from ₹1400/night. Rooftop terrace with fort panorama. Free WiFi, social common areas, staff arrange local walking tours, cooking classes, cooking workshops. Near Clock Tower, Sardar Market, Toorji step-well. Extremely popular — book 5–7 days ahead in season.

name: Suryagarh Palace
top_review: Suryagarh is a masterpiece. The architecture looks like a fort from outside but inside is pure luxury. Their curated desert experience is far superior to any camp. The folk music evenings under the stars are magical.
dietary_options: all dietary requirements on advance notice
text: Suryagarh Palace is Jaisalmer's premier luxury desert hotel on Sam Road. Rating 4.7/5 from 890 reviews. Rooms from ₹22,000/night. Fortress-style architecture with 100+ rooms, all elegantly furnished. Pool, Saffron restaurant (award-winning Rajasthani cuisine), Alaya Spa. Curated desert excursions include dune drives, sunset experiences, camel rides, folk performances. Private dining on dunes available. 15 km from city, 8 km from Sam Dunes. Voted among best desert hotels in India consistently.

name: Hotel Oasis
top_review: Excellent mid-budget option. Rooftop restaurant has stunning fort views at sunset. Staff arranged our camel safari and they negotiated good rates. Clean rooms, good hot water.
text: Hotel Oasis Jaisalmer is a reliable budget-to-mid hotel near the old city in Jaisalmer. Rating 4.2/5 from 1400+ reviews. Rooms from ₹900/night. Rooftop restaurant with fort views. Travel desk arranges camel safaris, desert camp packages, jeep excursions. Free WiFi, AC, hot water. Walking distance from Jaisalmer Fort, Patwon Ki Haveli, Gadisar Lake. Helpful staff who speak English well. Good value in a touristy area.

name: Sher Bagh Luxury Tented Camp
area: Adjacent to Ranthambore National Park Zone 1-4
top_review: The most extraordinary wildlife experience of our lives. Our naturalist guide Suresh spotted a tigress and three cubs within 20 minutes. The luxury tents are incredibly comfortable, food is farm-fresh, campfire evenings unforgettable.
text: Sher Bagh is Ranthambore's most celebrated luxury tented camp. Rating 4.8/5 from 620 reviews. All-inclusive packages from ₹28,000/person/night including safaris, meals, naturalist guides. 12 luxury canvas tents with wooden floors, en-suite bathrooms. Pool, campfire evenings, expert naturalists. Near Zone 1-4 for prime tiger territory. Organic kitchen using farm produce. Voted Best Wildlife Hotel in India by multiple publications. Book 3-4 months ahead for Oct-March season.

name: Hotel Hammir
top_review: Good mid-budget option. Safari booking was handled efficiently by hotel. Breakfast is solid. Rooms are clean and comfortable. Nothing extraordinary but reliable and well-priced.
text: Hotel Hammir is a reliable mid-range property on Ranthambore Road in Sawai Madhopur. Rating 4.1/5 from 890 reviews. Rooms from ₹3,500/night including breakfast. Safari zone permit booking assistance, travel desk. AC rooms, free WiFi, garden. 2 km from Ranthambore National Park main gate. Good restaurant serving Indian and local cuisine. Practical choice for safari-focused travellers who want comfort without luxury prices.

name: Bhanwar Singh Palace
top_review: Beautiful lake-view property with a spiritual atmosphere. The rooftop sunrise yoga overlooking the lake was the highlight of our trip. Food is excellent — try the lassi and dal. Peaceful and serene.
dietary_options: vegetarian only (Pushkar is a holy town)
text: Bhanwar Singh Palace is a heritage-style mid-range hotel in Pushkar near the sacred lake. Rating 4.3/5 from 760 reviews. Rooms from ₹3,200/night. Lake and Aravalli views from rooftop. Note: Pushkar is a holy town — hotel serves vegetarian food only and no alcohol. Rooftop sunrise yoga sessions, Ayurvedic massages, evening puja views. Short walk from Brahma Temple and Pushkar Ghats. Camel safari and desert excursion bookings arranged.

name: Hilltone Hotel
top_review: Best hotel in Mount Abu for the price. The views of the Aravalli hills from the garden are gorgeous. Pool is well-maintained. Good restaurant. Staff are extremely helpful.
text: Hilltone Hotel is a mid-range property in Mount Abu near Polo Ground. Rating 4.2/5 from 540 reviews. Rooms from ₹4,500/night. Pool, garden with Aravalli views, multi-cuisine restaurant. Mount Abu is Rajasthan's only hill station — pleasant year-round. Hotel is central for Dilwara Temples, Nakki Lake, Guru Shikhar. Good family option with space for kids.

name: Heritage stays and palace hotels
text: A heritage stay can be an experience in itself, but a palace-style name does not guarantee protected heritage, accessible rooms or included activities. Verify property identity, room location, lift/stairs, inclusions, cancellation and transport with the property. Compare total cost with a well-located independent hotel.

name: Desert camp selection
text: Before booking a desert camp, ask for its exact location, transport plan, tent type, bathroom facilities, heating/cooling, meal and performance inclusions, waste practices, cancellation terms and any animal rides. Confirm operator identity and safety arrangements. “Luxury” and “eco” are marketing labels; inspect specific inclusions.

name: Wildlife-trip accommodation logistics
text: Choose a wildlife-trip stay only after checking official safari reporting points and the operator’s pickup arrangements. Ask whether transfers are included, when they leave, and what happens if a permit or safari slot changes. No property can guarantee wildlife sightings or a particular zone.

name: Village stays and homestays
text: For a village homestay, confirm host identity, exact location, sanitation, meals, accessibility, payment/cancellation terms and transport before arrival. Ask what interaction is welcome; community visits should be consent-led and never treated as staged entertainment.
